tasks.title: Give each session phase its own fence and deny the bypasses the review found (F10, F6 fence part)
tasks.goal: The fence is the first line that saves attempts, and today one fence serves all three phases, allows Edit and Write everywhere but ~/.claude, and misses the git and find forms the review listed (brief F10 and F6's fence part). This task splits it into a plan, a work and a review fence and tightens all three, without taking away any command a skill tells a session to run. Later tasks make the driver the real boundary; the docs say plainly that the fence is advisory.

references.why: what a session never does and the fence it runs under; F10 adds that the fence is advisory, the driver the boundary, and that a consumer repo's .claude/settings.json allow rules also apply
S-2 and P-2: the commands each fence must keep denying so sessions never commit, move refs or set status
the B8 findings for F6 and F10 with the exact bypass forms and their evidence

acceptance: Each session phase is started with its own fence settings file: the plan, work and review sessions are not handed the same fence.
The plan fence allows writing .vloop/state/state.json and .vloop/tmp/**; the work and review fences allow writing nothing under .vloop/ but .vloop/tmp/**; all three deny Edit and Write on .git/**.

Every phase fence denies each form F10 lists: git -C . commit, git -c k=v push, git merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, pull, fetch, push to a URL, config, notes, replace, filter-branch, worktree, reflog, gc; find -delete, find -exec, find -fprint; git diff|log|show --output=…; rm -fr and rm -r -f; vloop -C . task set …; vloop brief new.
No deny rule of the v0.7.0 fence is dropped or narrowed in any phase fence.

internal/cli/fence_test.go holds TestFenceDeniesBypasses, which lists every F10 form and asserts each is denied by every phase fence's deny rules, and lists the allowed commands the skills use and asserts each is still allowed; and TestPhaseFenceWrites, which asserts each phase fence allows and denies the writes above.

TestPluginSkills judges each fenced skill against its own phase's fence and passes; TestEvalGrantsCoverFence checks the eval cases grant at least the work fence's allow list, and the eval cases and docs/guide/evals.md follow it.
No skill text changes beyond what F10 requires of the commands it names (brief: Out of scope).
docs/domain/execution/session.md says the fence is advisory, that the driver's checks are the boundary, and that a consumer repository's own .claude/settings.json allow rules also apply to sessions.

tasks.title: Make the driver's git ignore hooks and fsmonitor, and halt when .git/config, the hooks or a gate's refs change (F4, F5)
tasks.goal: A session can plant a git hook, core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor or a clean filter that then runs inside the driver's own commit, after the refs check; and a gate that commits or resets goes unnoticed (brief F4, F5). This task makes every git command the driver runs disable hooks and fsmonitor and read paths unquoted, hashes .git/config and the hooks directory around every session and gate, and snapshots refs around every gate, halting with exit 9 before anything is committed. It checks the outcome, not the command: the fence is not trusted here.

references.why: S-2 and R-3: sessions never move refs, and exit 9 is the halt this task widens to gates, .git/config and the hooks
the commits and endings of a run: nothing is committed on an exit-9 halt
what a session never does; the halt detects it after the fact
the F4 and F5 findings with their evidence

acceptance: Every git command the driver runs (plan, iterate, gates, preflight) passes -c core.hooksPath=<an empty directory under .vloop/tmp/>, -c core.fsmonitor=false and -c core.quotepath=false; no repository hook or fsmonitor runs on the driver's commits.

The driver hashes .git/config and the hooks directory that git rev-parse --git-path hooks names before each session and each gate; a change halts the run with exit 9 and the stderr line `vloop: <phase> changed .git/config — nothing was committed; restore it, then re-run` (or `the git hooks` in place of `.git/config`), and nothing is committed.

The driver snapshots refs before every gate run, the task's own and every regression gate, and halts with exit 9 and `vloop: the gate of <id> moved git refs — nothing was committed; restore them, then re-run` when they moved.
The preflight's pre-commit line reads exactly `  ! a pre-commit hook is active (<path>) — the driver's commits do not run repository hooks; put what it checks in the gates`.

cmd/vloop/run_git_test.go holds TestRunHooksPlanted (a work session writes .git/hooks/post-commit creating a branch: exit 9, the branch does not exist), TestRunGitConfigPlanted (a session adds [core] fsmonitor: exit 9) and TestRunGateMovesRefs (verify `git commit --allow-empty -qm x && true`: exit 9, no driver commit); each fails against the base.
The checks compare the state of .git/ and the refs before and after, not the commands a session ran (brief: Violations).

tasks.title: Keep the driver's inputs in memory, restore what a session changes among them, and run gates only from the plan the driver holds (F6 driver part, F7)
tasks.goal: A work session can zero cost_usd in earlier session records so the ceiling never fires, set model.review to weaken its own reviewer, change a defect, or rewrite a verify, run it with vloop task gate and put the plan back byte for byte (brief F6, F7). This task makes the driver sum spend from sessions as they finish, resolve model and effort once, hash and restore its inputs around each work and review session, and hand sessions VLOOP_PLAN_SHA256 so vloop task gate refuses a changed plan. Later tasks (review confinement) build on the same snapshot-and-restore shape.

references.why: S-2, P-2 and P-4: sessions do not change status or gates; the driver restores what they changed among its inputs
the session record and what a session never does; F6 restores records a session rewrote
the gate: who writes it and where it runs; F7 makes vloop task gate run only the plan the driver holds
budgets: the cost ceiling must fire on real spend, whatever is on disk
the F6 and F7 findings with their evidence

tasks.title: Time gates and sessions and leave nothing running (F3)
tasks.goal: Gates and sessions run with no deadline and no process group, and gate output is read through a pipe, so a gate that leaves a background server never returns and vloop run hangs forever while orphans pile up (brief F3). This task adds run.gate-timeout (15) and run.session-timeout (60), runs each gate and session in its own process group (a Job object on Windows), kills the group on timeout and when the gate's shell exits, and bounds the read of its output.

references.why: every config key is documented here with its default, values and variable; the two new keys join it
configuration and CLI conventions the new keys and their VLOOP_ variables follow
C-1 (config only in the repo, overridden by VLOOP_ variables) and R-3 (a timed-out session is exit 7)
budgets and endings, which gain the two timeouts
the gate: a timed-out gate is a failed gate

acceptance: New keys run.gate-timeout (default 15) and run.session-timeout (default 60), whole minutes, at least 1, with VLOOP_RUN_GATE_TIMEOUT and VLOOP_RUN_SESSION_TIMEOUT; an invalid value is a usage error (exit 2) on config set; config list and docs/guide/configuration.md show both.
Each gate and each session runs in its own process group (a Job object on Windows, in build-tagged files); on timeout the whole group is killed and a short wait bounds the read of its output.
A timed-out gate is a failed gate whose log ends with the line `vloop: gate <id> timed out after <n> min`; a timed-out session is a session error (exit 7).

When the gate's shell exits, anything left in its group is killed, so verify `sleep 1000 & exit 0` returns promptly through a pipe and leaves no sleep running — in the driver and in vloop task gate alike.

The timeout is injectable in tests in seconds; tests named TestGateLeavesNothingRunning, TestGateTimeout (a verify sleeping past a short test timeout fails with the line above) and TestSessionTimeout exist under internal/ and fail against the base.

tasks.title: Redact secret environment values and keep only tool and path of permission denials (F12)
tasks.goal: Gates run with the full environment and their output is committed in gates/*.log, so a test that dumps the environment commits ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; session records keep raw permission_denials whose inputs hold whole commands and file contents (brief F12). This task redacts the value of every secret-named environment variable before anything is written under .vloop/state/ and keeps only the tool name and file path of each denial.

references.why: the session record and its permission_denials field
C-3: the session record stays a valid session/v1 document
the F12 finding with its evidence

acceptance: Before anything is written under .vloop/state/ (gate logs, session records, reports, run.log, journal), every occurrence of the value of an environment variable whose name contains KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD or CREDENTIAL (case-insensitive) and whose value is at least 8 characters is replaced with `<redacted:NAME>`.
Redaction keys on variable names, not value shapes; a guide under docs/guide/ says what is redacted and that a secret in an innocently named variable is not caught.
Session records keep, per permission denial, the tool name and the file path when there is one — never the command or content — and still validate as session/v1.

tasks.title: Read handoffs only as regular files, take the lock atomically, and check the run id (F13)
tasks.goal: The driver reads .vloop/tmp/proposal.json and verdict.json through symlinks and copies a report into the committed run folder unvalidated, the lock is written through a link and is check-then-write, and a committed state.json's run_id is used in paths unchecked (brief F13). This task closes all three: no symlinked handoff, an exclusive-create lock, and a run_id that must match a pattern and the plan's brief.

references.why: the run folder and the lock this task hardens
C-3: state.v1.json is the schema the run_id pattern is added to
the F13 finding with its evidence

acceptance: Handoff files (proposal.json, verdict.json) are read only when they are regular files, never through a symlink; a symlinked one is treated as missing, and a report is copied into the run folder only after it validated.

The lock is created atomically with exclusive create and without following a symlink; a lock whose process is gone is replaced once; two concurrent acquisitions → exactly one succeeds and the other exits 1 naming the running pid.

run_id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, contain no .., and equal the run id of the plan's brief; otherwise vloop run exits 1 before anything is written. schemas/state.v1.json gains the pattern while still accepting the empty run_id a planning session writes.

internal/driver/safety_test.go holds TestLockExactlyOneOfConcurrent (two goroutines) and a test TestHandoffSymlinkIsMissing exists in internal/driver; cmd/vloop/run_tmp_test.go holds TestRunSymlinkedProposal (a proposal.json symlinked to a file holding SECRET: no SECRET under .vloop/state/) and TestRunBadRunID (run_id "../x": exit 1, nothing written outside the repo); each fails against the base.

tasks.title: Export repo.remote only as a URL or scp-like form without credentials, and never a local path (F14)
tasks.goal: repo.remote is exported as it is: a local remote leaks a path and a URL's query (?access_token=…) keeps a token, against M-7 (brief F14). This task exports the remote only as a URL or scp-like form without user info, query or fragment, and omits it for a local path or file:// remote.

references.why: M-7: an export carries no absolute paths and no credentials; C-3: export records stay valid export/v1
the F14 finding with its evidence

acceptance: A local path or file:// origin produces no remote field (absent, not null) and nothing in the repo identity names the path.

An https origin with user info, a query and a fragment is exported as https://<host>/<path> only, e.g. https://example.com/org/r.git; no token, user or fragment survives anywhere in the repo identity, including its name.
An ssh:// URL loses its user info; an scp-like origin keeps its host and path.
Every exported record still validates as export/v1.
internal/cli/export_test.go holds TestExportRemoteForms covering a temp-path origin and an https origin with user info and a query; it fails against the base.

tasks.title: Keep the machine awake for the lifetime of vloop run (C2)
tasks.goal: B7's acceptance run stalled when the machine slept (brief C2). This task adds run.keep-awake (on by default) and, while it is on, holds a no-idle-sleep hold for vloop run's own lifetime on macOS, Linux and Windows; failing to take the hold is one warning line in run.log, never a failure.

references.why: every config key is documented here; run.keep-awake joins it
configuration conventions: the key is an enum because config has no boolean type
C-1: the key lives in .vloop/config.toml with a VLOOP_ variable

acceptance: A new key run.keep-awake (on, off; default on; VLOOP_RUN_KEEP_AWAKE); another value is a usage error on config set; config list and docs/guide/configuration.md show it.

While on, vloop run holds a no-idle-sleep hold for its own lifetime: macOS `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` of vloop's own pid, Linux `systemd-inhibit --what=idle --why="vloop run" …` when available, Windows SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED); the hold ends when vloop run exits, however it exits.

If the hold cannot be taken, run.log gets exactly one line `vloop: could not keep the machine awake (<reason>) — a sleeping machine stalls the run` and the run continues; with run.keep-awake = off no hold is attempted.
docs/guide/concepts.md says what keep-awake does and that it does not cover closing a laptop's lid.

Tests TestKeepAwakeCommands (the command each OS would run, as pure functions, on every OS), TestKeepAwakeOff and the macOS-only TestCaffeinateExitsWithWatchedProcess exist under internal/ and fail against the base; OS-specific code is in build-tagged files.
